title: Using torch.optim ⚙️
description: Set up SGD and Adam, zero gradients, and step through parameter updates.

slides.title: The Training Step Loop 🔁
slides.content:
# Putting It All Together

```python
optimizer.zero_grad()
pred = model(input)
loss = criterion(pred, target)
loss.backward()
optimizer.step()
```

This is the core of every training loop. We'll practice with a tiny dataset.

slides.title: Full Training Step Example
slides.content: Train a linear regression model (1 feature → 1 output) with SGD.
slides.codeSnippet:
x = torch.tensor([[1.0], [2.0], [3.0]])
y = torch.tensor([[2.0], [4.0], [6.0]])  # y = 2x

model = nn.Linear(1, 1)
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
criterion = nn.MSELoss()

for epoch in range(5):
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    pred = model(x)
    loss = criterion(pred, y)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}: loss={loss.item():.4f}")

quizData.question: Which order is correct for a training iteration?
quizData.explanation: Always zero gradients, compute forward & loss, backward, then update.

slides.title: Adam Optimizer 🧠
slides.content:
## Adaptive Learning Rates

Adam combines momentum and adaptive per‑parameter learning rates. It's often the default choice:

`optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)`

It typically converges faster and is less sensitive to learning rate choice.

slides.title: Adam vs SGD Speed
slides.content: Compare Adam and SGD on the same linear problem (spoiler: Adam usually converges faster).
slides.codeSnippet:
# Using Adam
model_adam = nn.Linear(1, 1)
optimizer_adam = torch.optim.Adam(model_adam.parameters(), lr=0.1)
for epoch in range(5):
    optimizer_adam.zero_grad()
    loss = criterion(model_adam(x), y)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer_adam.step()
    print(f"Adam Epoch {epoch+1}: {loss.item():.4f}")

quizData.question: Why might Adam be preferred over vanilla SGD?

options.text: It adapts learning rates per parameter and often converges faster

quizData.explanation: Adam uses momentum and adaptive rates, making it robust and fast for many tasks.

slides.title: ⚠️ Zero Grad Every Iteration
slides.content:
## Don't Forget zero_grad()!

If you forget, gradients accumulate from multiple batches, leading to erratic updates. Always call `optimizer.zero_grad()` before `loss.backward()`.
